newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Palace on Tuesday admitted that it was behind the signature drive for a people's initiative to amend the Constitution. (INQUIRER)

- President Ramos returns to Manila on Wednesday from what he described as an "astoundingly successful" ten-day visit to five countries in south Asia and the Persian Gulf, saying his sojourn has put the Philippines on the map of foreign investors in this part of the world. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- It's censure, not suspension, for Representative Romeo Jalosjos for his conduct during the 23 days he was evading arrest on charges of statutory rape. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Lower House and Finance officials are eyeing a compromise formula to lower the tax exemption brackets that were approved by the House Committee on ways and means. The Committee wanted all people earning below 184,000 pesos annually to be exempt from income tax and finance officials want it lowered. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Former Philippine Stock Exchange president Vitaliano Nanagas admitted that he moved too fast too soon in implementing reforms to professionalise the bourse. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Two of the country's largest organizations of advertisers on Tuesday said they will temporarily stop placing any commercials with the Lopez-controlled ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp to forestall plans by the television network to increase advertising rates.
